jobs.title: Clinical Product & Operations Lead Pharmacist
jobs.description:
Develop Health is on a mission to use AI to radically accelerate access to life-saving medications. By automating complex, manual healthcare processes—like benefit verification and prior authorization— we've been growing rapidly and over the past couple of years have helped over 2.5 million patients!

We’re partnering with some of the largest pharmacy benefit managers and payers in the nation, revolutionizing how healthcare interactions occur by eliminating human delays and inefficiencies. Our small, elite team of founders and engineers have previously launched and exited successful healthcare startups including Rupa Health and Canvas Medical. We are now scaling rapidly following a major funding round.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re hiring a Clinical Product & Operations Lead Pharmacist to be the clinical anchor of our customer experience. You’ll be the person customers reach when a prior authorization or benefit verification case gets hard, and the person our product and engineering teams turn to when they need to know how the work actually happens.

This is an individual contributor role for a licensed pharmacist who can own moderate-to-complex cases end to end and build the workflows around them. Your time splits across two connected jobs: supporting customers directly on tough cases, and designing the operational processes, internal and customer-facing, that hold quality high as we scale.

We’re looking for someone as comfortable on a customer call as they are writing an SOP or sitting with an engineer to explain why a payer criterion matters. Expect startup pace, real ambiguity, and a lot of ownership. This role is based in our Menlo Park office at least three days per week.




WHAT YOU'LL DO – IMPACT IN YOUR FIRST 3–6 MONTHS

 - Own customer support for moderate-to-complex prior authorization and benefit verification cases, serving as the primary point of contact for escalations and providing clear clinical context, status, and a path to resolution.

 - Apply clinical judgment to navigate payer criteria, formulary requirements, and appeals on the cases staff can’t resolve on their own.

 - Build the support foundations: document workflows, write playbooks and SOPs, and turn one-off fixes into repeatable processes.

 - Be the voice of the customer with product and engineering. Surface patterns in where customers get stuck, flag errors in AI-generated determinations, and help prioritize what gets fixed.

 - Work directly with engineering to make our AI agents better at real casework: feeding hard PA and BV cases back into the product, flagging where determinations go wrong, and shaping the agentic workflows that handle them.

 - Manage customer communication across email, calls, and Slack with clarity and care, especially in high-stakes patient situations.




WHAT YOU'LL OWN – DRIVING GROWTH BEYOND 12 MONTHS

 - Own the operational playbook for how complex PA and BV cases get handled, internally and for customers, and keep it current as payer rules change.

 - Build and track the metrics that show impact: resolution time, approval rates, and where automation helps versus where it still breaks.

 - Become a defining voice in how the product evolves by translating what you see in support into high-leverage improvements.

 - Design and scale training so new pharmacists and technicians ramp fast and hold the same quality bar.

 - Help shape how the pharmacy operations and support function works as we expand across payers, PBMs, and enterprise partners.

 - Partner with engineering to push more complex casework onto AI agents: deciding what to automate next, where a human still needs to be in the loop, and how to keep quality high as the agents take on more.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING ON DAY 1

 - Licensed pharmacist (PharmD) with hands-on prior authorization and benefit verification experience.

 - 3–5+ years in pharmacy operations, specialty pharmacy, or a payer/PBM environment.

 - Strong working knowledge of PA workflows, payer criteria, formularies, and PBM structures, enough to handle moderate-to-complex cases on your own.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication, including real customer-facing experience explaining clinical concepts simply.

 - Comfort working cross-functionally with product, engineering, and operations in a fast-paced startup.

 - Availability to work on-site in Menlo Park at least three days per week.




WHAT YOU'LL NEED TO LEARN QUICKLY

 - How Develop Health’s platform and automation fit into real payer/PBM processes, and where the product creates leverage in customer operations.

 - Our internal escalation paths and engineering workflows, and how to raise an issue so it gets resolved fast.

 - How different payers interpret PA and BV requirements, and how those differences show up in customer experience.

 - How our AI generates clinical responses and determinations, so you can review them and give engineers feedback they can act on.




BONUS POINTS

 - Experience building QA processes or supervising pharmacists and technicians.

 - Deep understanding of the patient access journey, from prescription to dispensing, including common failure modes and payer friction.

 - Comfort using AI tools to work faster day to day.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - $170,000–$220,000 base salary plus meaningful early-stage equity.

 - Health, dental, and vision coverage; flexible PTO.

 - High-end workstation & tooling budget.

 - The chance to make medication access dramatically faster for hundreds of thousands of patients every month.

jobs.title: Strategic Business Operations Lead
jobs.description:
Develop Health is on a mission to use AI to radically accelerate access to life-saving medications. By automating complex, manual healthcare processes—like benefit verification and prior authorization— we've been growing rapidly and over the past couple of years have helped over 2.5 million patients!

We’re partnering with some of the largest pharmacy benefit managers and payers in the nation, revolutionizing how healthcare interactions occur by eliminating human delays and inefficiencies. Our small, elite team of founders and engineers have previously launched and exited successful healthcare startups including Rupa Health and Canvas Medical. We are now scaling rapidly following a major funding round.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring a Strategic Business Operations Lead to make sure every new strategic account actually runs well once it's signed.

A new payer or PBM partnership goes live and a dozen operational questions come with it. Who works the queue. What the SLA is. Which cases need a human and which the product should handle. What "good" looks like in the numbers. You'll be the person who answers those questions, then builds the systems so nobody has to ask them again.

Day to day that means working real benefit verification and prior authorization cases, finding where workflows break, and turning each fix into a documented process the team can run without you. You'll also help manage our BPO partners, keep the daily queue moving, and build the dashboards leadership uses to see how operations are performing.

The unusual part: our product is the automation. A lot of this job is spotting work our AI should be doing and getting it in front of product and engineering with enough detail to build.

You'll report to our Head of Pharmacy Operations and PBM Relations. Much of our operational playbook is still being written, so you'll have a lot of latitude and a lot of blank pages.




WHAT YOU'LL DO — IMPACT IN YOUR FIRST 3–6 MONTHS

 - Run the work. Take on complex benefit verification and prior authorization cases and become the person the team trusts to untangle them.

 - Find and fix what's broken. Track down workflow bottlenecks, payer and PBM issues, and process gaps that slow the team down or frustrate customers.

 - Write things down. Turn what you learn into workflow docs, playbooks, and repeatable processes that hold up as volume grows.

 - Feed product and engineering. Bring customer pain points back with enough specificity to prioritize, and flag where automation could replace manual work.

 - Level up the team. Build the training materials and knowledge resources that cut escalations.




WHAT YOU'LL OWN — DRIVING GROWTH BEYOND 6 MONTHS

 - Support our BPO partnerships. Be the day-to-day contact for our outsourcing partners, hold them to quality standards, and drive improvements in service delivery.

 - Help plan capacity. Forecast volume, flag coverage gaps across time zones, and help onboard new team members as we hire.

 - Build the reporting. Own the operational metrics, SLA dashboards, and performance analytics that leadership uses to make decisions.

 - Keep the queue healthy. Balance incoming demand against team capacity so wait times stay low and SLAs hold as we scale.

 - Turn insight into leverage. Convert frontline patterns into product and process changes that cut support volume and improve unit economics.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING ON DAY 1

 - 2–4 years in operations, ideally in healthcare, health tech, or SaaS.

 - Composure under pressure. You've handled complex, high-stakes work and can keep everyone calm through it.

 - Strong analytical instincts. You pull your own data and build your own dashboards and reports.

 - A root-cause habit. You investigate, spot patterns, and fix the system rather than the symptom.

 - Comfort with ambiguity. You've worked somewhere the process didn't exist yet, and you built it.




WHAT YOU'LL NEED TO LEARN QUICKLY

 - Our domain and product: how our workflows and automation layer map onto real payer, PBM, and provider processes, and where the product creates leverage.

 - How we operate: our escalation paths and engineering workflows, and how to raise an issue so it gets resolved fast.

 - Payer nuance: how different payers interpret prior authorization and benefit verification requirements, and what those differences mean for customers.




BONUS POINTS

 - Hands-on experience with pharmacy benefit prior authorization or benefit verification on the payer or PBM side.

 - A strong grasp of the patient access journey from prescription to dispensing, including where payers create friction.

 - You've built support processes, documentation, or training from scratch before.

 - Familiarity with AI tooling, BPO workforce management software, or BI and reporting platforms.




THIS MIGHT NOT BE THE RIGHT FIT IF

 - You want to manage a team on day one. This role builds the systems and runs the work. People management may come as we scale, but it isn't the job today.

 - You'd rather stay out of the queue. Your credibility here comes from working real cases yourself, not from reviewing someone else's summary of them.

 - You want a playbook. Most of ours is still unwritten, and writing it is a large part of the role.

 - You want to hand the analysis to someone else. You'll build your own dashboards and pull your own data.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Competitive base salary plus meaningful early-stage equity.

 - Health, dental, and vision coverage, and flexible PTO.

 - High-end workstation and AI tooling budget.

 - Work that makes medication access dramatically faster for hundreds of thousands of patients a month, with room to grow as the operations function scales.

If you're passionate about building meaningful technology in healthcare, we'd love to hear from you.
